subject: Order form: liability caps, OSS pass-throughs, and model licensing questions
messages:
From: Sofia Navarro <sofia.navarro@luminai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@luminai.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form: liability caps & OSS pass-throughs

Evelyn/Team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at LuminAI is reviewing the draft order form and MSA. A couple legal items bubbled up that we need clarified before we move to signature: 

1) Liability cap — your MSA currently references a general cap but LuminAI needs confirmation on the Order Form-specific cap and whether certain carve-outs (IP infringement, data breach) flow outside that cap.

2) OSS / model licensing — our legal team sees potential third-party claims tied to the open-source models and licenses used in the deployed artifacts. We're asking for (a) a pass-through indemnity for third-party claims that come directly from OSS licensors and (b) visibility into any limits on that pass-through.

3) Consequential damages — preference is mutual exclusion, but we need to know if model-related downstream losses (e.g., regulatory fines tied to model outputs) are being carved out.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and share a redline or proposed language? We have an internal procurement approval meeting on Friday and would like to have proposed contract language by Thursday EOD.

Attachments: vendor_requirements_202601.pdf (procurement checklist)

Best,
Sofia Navarro
Sr. Procurement Manager, LuminAI

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Navarro <sofia.navarro@luminai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: liability caps & OSS pass-throughs

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear summary. Quick reply while we pull legal in.

High-level positions we can take now:
- Order Form liability cap: propose cap = greater of (12 months of fees paid under the Order Form) or $2,000,000. We can consider a higher cap for enterprise/negotiated deals.
- Carve-outs: Standard carve-outs for fraud and gross negligence; IP infringement claims (including third-party OSS license claims) should be addressed via a limited pass-through indemnity rather than removing them entirely from the cap.
- OSS pass-through: we can accept a flow-down for direct third-party claims where a licensor asserts breach of license obligations tied to code/models we deliver — but limit pass-through to (a) amounts actually awarded or paid to third parties and (b) defense costs, and subject to notice/defense cooperation provisions. We do not want open-ended liability for consequential/regulatory fines arising solely from customer deployment choices.

I'm looping in Rishi to propose specific redline language for the OSS pass-through and for the Order Form cap. Marcus — can you confirm whether any model vendor agreements we rely on already require specific pass-through terms?

We should target a redline back to you by Thursday EOD.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0191

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Navarro <sofia.navarro@luminai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order form: liability caps & OSS pass-throughs

Team / Sofia — attaching a short note with suggested redline snippets (attached). Key legal points: 

- OSS "third-party license claims" (defined) — we can accept pass-through of obligations to the extent those claims are the direct result of Redwood's distribution of specific OSS artifacts or model weights we supplied (not for customer modifications or end-use). Pass-through relief should be limited to: (i) amounts actually paid to settle or under final judgment; and (ii) Redwood's reasonable defense costs.

- We recommend adding strict procedural conditions: prompt written notice of claim, sole control of defense by Redwood with right for customer to participate at its own expense, and inability to settle without mutual consent if settlement imposes indemnified obligations on the other party.

- Cap interaction: Order Form cap should apply to all liabilities except those that by law cannot be limited. For IP infringement claims we suggest moving to a separate sub-cap: where IP/OSS pass-through applies, limit Redwood's exposure to the lesser of the Order Form cap or the direct amounts paid to third parties plus defense costs. This prevents opening the general cap to unlimited third-party statutory damages.

- Consequential damages: preserve mutual exclusion. For regulatory fines tied to customer conduct (e.g., using model outputs improperly), the customer should remain responsible. We can agree to indemnify for claims that are purely traceable to Redwood's negligent model training that violated a specific warranty, but that's narrow.

I'll attach redline snippets now. If you want, I can convert these to tracked changes in the draft_orderform_redlines_v1.docx.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Evelyn/Rishi — thanks for the prompt response and the proposed approach. A few follow-ups from our counsel: 

- They want explicit language that the pass-through can be flow-downed to our subs and service providers (we use multiple vendors). Is Redwood comfortable confirming pass-through will reach downstream subcontractors that have direct licensing obligations to the OSS licensors?

- They also asked whether Redwood carries cyber liability insurance that would cover third-party IP claims arising from your hosted service (we can share our policy requirements if helpful).

- Finally, procurement prefers that "defense costs" include reasonable attorneys' fees rather than being narrowly limited to court costs.

We've uploaded our vendor requirements checklist (vendor_requirements_202601.pdf) to the Drive link and flagged a few clauses for your review. Can you get an answer on subcontractor flow-down and insurance by Thursday? We need to make a procurement recommendation.

Best,
Sofia

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: liability caps & OSS pass-throughs

Sofia — appreciate the quick follow-ups. Summary of Redwood positions and next steps: 

1) Subcontractor flow-down: Redwood will accept that any pass-through indemnity for third-party OSS license claims may be flow-downed to Redwood's authorized subcontractors (i.e., those vendors that directly ship or host the relevant OSS artifacts) provided Redwood remains the coordinating party for claims and the subcontractor obligations are limited to the same scope and caps. We will not accept a model where each subcontractor can independently enlarge Redwood's cap.

2) Insurance: Redwood carries a commercial general liability and technology errors & omissions policy; we will provide certificate of insurance showing $2M limits and cyber/E&O coverage details upon request. If LuminAI needs higher limits as a commercial term, we can discuss as part of the Order Form options.

3) Defense costs: we agree to include "reasonable attorneys' fees" as part of defense costs for covered OSS pass-through claims (subject to the usual cooperation and control mechanics).

4) Proposed cap language for the Order Form: "The aggregate liability of Redwood arising under or relating to this Order Form shall not exceed the greater of (i) the total fees paid to Redwood under this Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim; or (ii) two million dollars (USD $2,000,000), except to the extent such liabilities cannot be limited by applicable law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, third-party OSS license claims accepted as pass-through indemnity shall be recoverable only to the extent of amounts actually paid to third parties and Redwood's reasonable defense costs, and shall not expand Redwood's aggregate cap beyond the amounts stated above."

Next steps: Rishi will turn the suggested snippets into tracked changes on draft_orderform_redlines_v1.docx and share a Drive link. We can target a response back to LuminAI with tracked changes by Thursday EOD and follow up on insurance certificate.

Thanks — Evelyn
